clue.text: Here some shell out pounds for foreign bread

definitions.text: Here some shell out pounds for foreign bread

parts.words: Here some shell out pounds for foreign bread
parts.note: a place where travellers hand over sterling and receive another country's money, 'bread' being slang for cash rather than a loaf

explanation.surface: Tourists paying good money for a fancy continental loaf at a bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell out pounds' sounds like spending at a shop and 'bread' like food; in fact pounds are sterling and bread is slang for money, so the place swaps one currency for another.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiosk where currency is exchanged is precisely where people hand over sterling to get spending money for abroad.

clue.text: Someone who is getting on, not a day boy

explanation.surface: A pupil who lives at school, or a passenger stepping aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A boarder gets on a ship, bus or train; at school a boarder lives in, unlike a pupil who goes home daily.

clue.text: A daring Eurocrat involved in an attempt to avert defeat

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of a daring Eurocrat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bold Brussels official caught up in a last-ditch defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard action is literally a fight by troops at the back of a retreating army, and figuratively a last-ditch resistance.

clue.text: Cross, like the 'irsute Esau

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Cross, like the 'irsute Esau (4)' for AIRY: like the 'irsute Esau gives 'AIRY (hairy without H), but 'Cross' does not define AIRY and no source gives a different printed wording

clue.text: Mothers regularly taking fruit

parts.note: dams are animal mothers, as in horse breeding
being on a drug or medicine means regularly taking it

explanation.surface: Mums routinely eating a certain fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but alternate letters of Mothers will not help; 'on' as in 'on medication' means regularly taking.
explanation.definitionFit: A damson is a small dark plum.

clue.text: Signs of respect from short little girl full of energy

parts.note: curt means short in manner, brusque

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the little girl holds the energy symbol

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a little girl
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Gestures of respect from a small, very lively girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsy is the bob made by bending the knees to honour royalty or a superior.

clue.text: Hit on a plan to change sort of service book in church

definitions.text: sort of service book in church

indicators.note: to change says the letters of hit on a plan must be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Coming up with an idea to reform how worship is conducted.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a book of the responses sung alternately by two halves of a choir in church services.

clue.text: Book launched by means of puff?

definitions.text: Book launched by means of puff?

parts.words: Book launched by means of puff?
parts.note: puff suggests publicity hype for a new novel, but read as a gust of air it sends something off on the breeze, giving a famous novel's title

explanation.surface: A novel promoted on the strength of hype.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puff' is publishing slang for promotional blurb; read literally it is a breath of air that carries something away, which is the title of Margaret Mitchell's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Mitchell's American Civil War novel bears a title describing something carried away by a breeze.

clue.text: Bit of a revolution is what university student wants

explanation.surface: A small part of an uprising, or the goal of an undergraduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests politics, but it is a full turn of 360 units.
explanation.definitionFit: One three-hundred-and-sixtieth of a full rotation is the angular unit; it is also the academic award a graduate earns.

clue.text: New arrangement in an Indian city backed by millions

indicators.note: backed by means supported from behind, so the millions abbreviation comes after the city

parts.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A fresh plan in an Indian city, financed by millions.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by rearranging another's letters is literally a reordering of them, i.e. a fresh ordering.

clue.text: When confused, reunite with the people behind

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled, so the word reunite is rearranged

explanation.surface: Muddled people meeting up again with their supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants who follow behind an important person.

clue.text: Scoundrel brought before English magistrate

indicators.note: brought before places the scoundrel word ahead of the abbreviation for English

parts.note: a dog is an old word for a contemptible man, a cur

explanation.surface: A villain hauled up in front of an English JP.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a court appearance; the Doge was the chief magistrate of the old republics of Venice and Genoa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doge was the elected chief magistrate who ruled Venice and Genoa.

clue.text: Hack's capacity for work?

parts.note: a hack here is a riding horse, not a journalist, and its working strength gives the name of a unit of engine output

explanation.surface: How much copy a jobbing journalist can turn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' suggests a journalist, but it is a horse let out for hire; the unit of power is named after what a horse can do.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit measuring an engine's rate of work was defined by comparison with a draught animal's pulling effort.

clue.text: Nice carton specially made for instrument

indicators.note: specially made means put together in a new form, so the letters of nice carton are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasant box is custom-built to hold an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A concertina is a small hexagonal squeezebox, an accordion-like musical instrument.

clue.text: Grounds are churned up by boy

indicators.note: churned up means stirred about, so the letters of are are rearranged

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A pitch torn up by a lad playing on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds in the sense of a justification or motive for doing something.

clue.text: Eastern drink dumped in river — one our folk don't want?

indicators.note: dumped in means thrown into, so the eastern drink goes inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone tipped a bottle of oriental liquor into the river, an unwelcome act.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: someone expelled is a person a nation does not want.
explanation.definitionFit: A person expelled from a country is someone its government has decided should not stay.

clue.text: Metal coating no good — useless material, primarily

indicators.note: no means without, so the good abbreviation is taken out

parts.note: plating is a thin coating of metal

indicators.note: primarily means at the start, so the first letters of useless and material are taken

explanation.surface: A metal coating that's no good is chiefly worthless stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' takes G from PLATING, leaving PLATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a precious silvery-white metallic element.

clue.text: Contempt about to be shown by dictator in power

indicators.note: in places the dictator and the about abbreviation inside the word for power

parts.note: to rule is to hold power, and rule means authority

indicators.note: shown by means displayed beside, so the about abbreviation follows the dictator

parts.note: Idi Amin was the Ugandan dictator, a crossword regular
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Scorn is due as a despot in office is about to be exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridicule is mockery that treats someone with scorn.

clue.text: Dram or possibly something one could get in a barrel

definitions.text: something one could get in a barrel

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of dram or might be put into another order

explanation.surface: A tot of whisky, or perhaps something tapped from a cask.
explanation.walkthrough: The barrel is a gun's, not a cask; a ramrod is pushed down a muzzle-loader's barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramrod is the rod used to ram the charge down the barrel of a muzzle-loading gun.

clue.text: Scheme needing diplomacy by one Conservative

parts.note: tact is sensitivity and diplomacy in dealing with people
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A plan that needs the delicate touch of a single Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a plan or manoeuvre designed to achieve an end.

clue.text: Threaded loops, a hundred on church vestment

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the hundred comes before the vestment

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a rochet is a white linen vestment worn by bishops

explanation.surface: Lacework of looped thread, worth a hundred, sewn onto a cleric's robe.
explanation.definitionFit: Crochet is needlework made by drawing yarn through loops with a hooked needle.

clue.text: Cross about church being insincere?

indicators.note: about means around, so the river crossing surrounds the church abbreviation

parts.note: to ford is to cross a river by wading
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Being angry with the church seems put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, but it is the verb to ford a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A forced smile or laugh is strained and artificial, not genuinely felt.

clue.text: Staff given allowance in softening-up process

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff of office
a ration is a fixed allowance of food or supplies

explanation.surface: Employees receive a pay allowance in an effort to sweeten them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees and 'softening-up' as persuasion; maceration is literally softening by soaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Maceration is the soaking of a substance in liquid until it becomes soft.

clue.text: What may account for some wild emotionalism?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asking what explains a bout of unrestrained feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: a protest rally is the kind of event that would explain outbursts of passion.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest march is a likely cause behind a crowd's heated displays of feeling.

clue.text: Component of alphabet (Athenian)

indicators.note: a component is a part, so the letters are found as part of the words alphabet and Athenian

explanation.surface: A letter in the Greek writing system.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the run sits across the end of alphabet and the start of Athenian, and the letter is part of the Athenian alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, used in Athens.

clue.text: Work at home I love — craftsman's ultimate judgement

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
in means at home
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as a zero

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so the final letter of craftsman's is taken

explanation.surface: Working from home, I adore the finished verdict of a skilled artisan.
explanation.definitionFit: A view or assessment formed about something is a judgement.

clue.text: To be fond of the woman is hard after first sign of cruelty

indicators.note: after places the woman, is and hard following the first letter of cruelty
the first sign of a word is its opening letter, here the start of cruelty

parts.note: her refers to a woman
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Loving a woman is difficult once she shows her first hint of cruelty.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish someone is to hold them dear and treat them with tenderness.

clue.text: Ted, debonair man playing a fruit-machine

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A suave fellow called Ted gambles on a slot machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' is the anagram indicator, and the surface makes it Ted playing the machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot machine with a pull lever is nicknamed for its single arm and its habit of robbing players.
